method: Loaded exact packet JSON and existing batch.decode only; never load_packet. Read frozen original, actor, own-term and search evidence. Visually examined complete original pages in supplied GPO PDF, complete EO 317A parent, EO 418 parent and Canal actors EO 474, EO 506, EO 1250 and EO 1372. Date, subject and signature checked against allowed identity crosswalk. Number identity is crosswalk-dependent: the printing has no EO numbers. These records assess source sufficiency and approve no unprovided claim.
shared_limits: Whole-case first cessation/current predicate remains distinct from original existence and provisional NO. No status adoption, human certification, filing or publication.

Frozen number-citation USC searches cover edition through 2026-10-09, leaving laws enacted October 10-14 outside that edition. eCFR/49-title bulk searches are bounded number-reference searches. OFR disposition catalog begins 1937 and cannot alone exclude earlier cessation of these 1904-1911 orders. Search complete means the machine operation finished, not that legal history is complete.

Person-name searches cover held EO texts only, omit 85 orders without held texts and disclose 302 of 2246 one-person orders without parsable names. Zero hits do not establish appointment, transfer, death, retirement or cessation.

No native claim byte-verification pass is inferred for these dossiers. Original text SHA pins are separately checked and the supplied raw GPO PDF was hashed and viewed. Original raw source references in the native format lack explicit raw_path.

No raw actor PDF was supplied with a usable path for EO 9830, EO 8393 or EO 1532. No claim of viewing those absent actor bytes. EO 9830 opening/Part III/signature OCR and EO 8393/EO 1532 frozen contexts are leads only. Packet actor-texts/EO_9830.json overflow path is absent.

unresolved_questions: Locate first ending/replacement of the continuing sale/notice/residue regime and exact effective date.
Resolve pending property sales and held residues; a computed 1911 anniversary would be unsupported without transaction evidence and still would not end the recurring order.
